record.paper_title: Cyber-Physical Attacks on UAS Networks–Challenges and Open Research Problems
record.original_question: Under what conditions can an adversary defeat beamforming antenna arrays in a UAS network by deceiving direction-of-arrival estimation or manipulating distributed beamnulling so that legitimate links are nulled, and what countermeasures can prevent the beamnulling process from converging toward a disconnected network state?

evidence.quote: An adversary may attack the DoA estimator by shaping its jamming signals to mimic waveforms of a nearby legitimate node, thus avoiding detection or causing false detections.

In certain conditions, the adversary can maximize the efficiency of jamming attacks by persistently manipulating the distributed beamnulling mechanism in such a way that its solution converges towards a maximally disconnected state. Analytical studies into feasibility criteria of this attack may produce insights into possible countermeasures and mitigation techniques.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a network of $N$ nodes (e.g., aerial platforms) located at positions $\{x_i\}_{i=1}^N \subset \mathbb{R}^3$, each equipped with an antenna array capable of adaptive beamforming and beamnulling. Each node $i$ estimates the direction-of-arrival (DoA) $\hat{\theta}_{ij}$ of incoming signals from neighbours $j$ and from a putative jammer, and steers a spatial null toward the estimated jammer direction while keeping legitimate neighbour directions in its main lobe. The set of links active at time $t$ defines a communication graph $G(t)$.

Suppose an adversary controls one (or several) jamming transmitters that can: (i) shape their emitted waveforms to mimic those of legitimate nodes so as to bias each node's DoA estimator $\hat{\theta}$; and (ii) move and re-emit over time so as to drive the iterative distributed beamnulling update rule of the network into a fixed point in which the connectivity of $G(t)$ is minimised (ideally, $G$ becomes disconnected).

Formalise this setting as a dynamical game between the adversary's signal/trajectory policy and the network's distributed beamnulling update, and answer the following:

1. Give precise analytical conditions (on geometry, array beamwidth, DoA-estimator noise model, mimicry capability, and adversary mobility) under which the adversary can force the DoA estimates at a positive fraction of nodes to deviate by more than the half-power beamwidth, thereby causing legitimate links to be nulled.

2. Characterise feasibility criteria — necessary and sufficient — under which a persistent adversarial input can drive the distributed beamnulling iteration to converge to a maximally disconnected configuration of $G$.

3. Design a distributed update rule (with provable guarantees) that prevents convergence of the beamnulling process toward any disconnected state, and quantify the connectivity it preserves as a function of the adversary's power, mobility, and mimicry fidelity.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent works on distributed adaptive beam-nulling in 3D UAV mesh networks (e.g., Bhunia et al., 2017–2018) propose Kalman-filter-based jammer tracking and adaptive beamnulling, and recent multi-agent reinforcement-learning approaches model UAV anti-jamming as a potential game with Nash equilibria. However, no published work provides full analytical feasibility criteria for an adversary to drive distributed beamnulling to a maximally disconnected state, nor a distributed update rule with provable guarantees against such convergence. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Distributed adaptive beam nulling to survive against jamming in 3D UAV mesh networks
status_evidence.snippet: Adaptive beamnulling antenna spatially filters out signals from a given direction; Kalman-filter tracking estimates jammer trajectory.
status_evidence.claim: Partial mitigation techniques exist but do not analytically characterize adversarial convergence to disconnected states.

status_evidence.title: Agent-Based Anti-Jamming Techniques for UAV Networks
status_evidence.snippet: UAV anti-jamming modeled as local interaction Markov game / potential game with Nash equilibria.
status_evidence.claim: Recent learning-theoretic approaches address anti-jamming but not the specific feasibility/countermeasure question for beamnulling-induced disconnection.

status_evidence.title: Distributed Adaptive Beam Nulling to Mitigate Jamming in 3D UAV Mesh Networks
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a distributed adaptive beam-nulling scheme with jammer tracking, without proving robustness against adversarial DoA-deception attacks driving the network to disconnection.
status_evidence.claim: Existing schemes do not analytically rule out adversarial convergence to maximally disconnected states.
